# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — code-enforce payment arg-fill + enriched write returns + execute-on-confirmation prompt rule
- Changes I made (1 line per edit; file/tool + cluster):
  - tools.py `_normalize_payment_methods` (new helper) + `book_reservation` rewrite: coerce `id`→`payment_id`, drop junk keys, and for a SINGLE payment method auto-fill `amount = total_price`. [cluster 2: payment arg mis-fill / amount errors]
  - tools.py `book_reservation`: richer errors (payment not found → Available:[...]; amount does not add up → sum to exactly X; insufficient balance shows balance/needed) + enriched dict return (amount_charged, payment_summary). [clusters 2, 3]
  - tools.py `update_reservation_flights`: enriched return amount_charged/amount_refunded/new_flights_total_price/payment_summary (already ×passengers). [cluster 3: wrong communicated amount]
  - tools.py `update_reservation_baggages`: enriched return amount_charged/payment_summary. [cluster 3]
  - tools.py docstrings (book/update): literal per-param JSON examples for flights/payment_methods/cabin. [cluster 2]
  - policy.md +3 additive sections: "Executing a confirmed action" (write the same turn as the go-ahead, no extra message), "Recovering from a tool error" (self-correct + re-call), "Reporting amounts" (per-passenger; read amount_* verbatim). [clusters 1, 3]
- Per change, EXPECTED effect + why safe:
  - Payment normalize/auto-fill should let tasks 8/12/25 book in one call instead of stalling on schema/amount errors; SAFE because it is a no-op when a single amount is already correct (verified: credit_card amount=150 unchanged) and multi-method wrong sums still error.
  - Enriched returns should fix the wrong-refund communicate miss on 11/12 (verified GV1N64 refund=5244 not 1748); SAFE because they only add fields, DB state unchanged, and to_json_str serializes dicts fine.
  - Execute-on-confirmation rule targets the no-write stall (8/12/17/19/25/40); SAFE because passing tasks already act after "yes" and the rule flips no act/refuse decision.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — iteration 1, LEDGER/RUNMAP/rejected.jsonl empty.
- Refuted hypotheses: none recorded yet.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: task 22 wrong-reservation-id selection (needs route-matching guard — not attempted, risk of overfit); cabin-vs-cancel decision (task 11 t0) — ambiguous decision rule, left untouched.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration).
- Focus next iteration: measure this batch's RESULT; if the no-write stall persists despite the prompt rule, escalate cluster 1 to a code lever (composite atomic write) per the tools skill's `narrated_without_action` row — a prose reminder on that class is expected to be weak. Then consider a route-matching resolver for task 22.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.483 Δ=+0.200 · fixed={—} · broke={—} · unresolved={11, 12, 17, 25, 37, 8} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).
<!-- cand_0001: ACCEPTED val=0.483 Δ=+0.200 -->

## Iteration cand_0002 — route-match reservation tool + cancel/passenger code guards + targeted policy rules
- Changes I made (1 line per edit; file/tool + cluster):
  - tools.py NEW `list_reservations(user_id)` loop tool — returns each reservation's human route ("Newark (EWR) -> Chicago (ORD)"), cabin, dates, passengers. [cluster 1: wrong-reservation selection, tasks 17/22]
  - tools.py `cancel_reservation` in-body guard — raise if any segment date < current date (flown → transfer needed). [cluster 2: cancel eligibility, task 37]
  - tools.py `update_reservation_passengers` — accept partial passenger dicts, auto-fill missing `dob` positionally from the existing reservation, actionable count-mismatch error. [cluster 3: name-change stall, task 40]
  - policy.md Modify flight: ordered "Finding the right reservation" procedure (list_reservations → match route/cities → "already-satisfied change = wrong reservation" → ask if ambiguous) + worked example. [17/22]
  - policy.md Change passengers: reuse unchanged fields via get_reservation_details; don't ask/transfer for a fetchable dob. [40]
  - policy.md Cancel flight: eligibility gate before cancel; never cancel flown; finish permitted writes before transferring. [37]
  - policy.md Executing a confirmed action: a conditional go-ahead counts once its condition is settled (gated behind confirmed eligibility); present one summary early. [19]
  - policy.md Book flight: "same flight as before" → read prior reservation, don't guess from times; "cheapest" → enumerate all options, pick min-total. [8 t1, 23 t2]
- Per change, EXPECTED effect + why safe:
  - `list_reservations` + route-match rule should make 17/22 operate on FQ8APE (the only Chicago-destination reservation) instead of the first (UM3OG5). SAFE: new READ tool + additive prose; single-reservation tasks and the untouched write paths of passing 11/25 are unaffected (verified identical output).
  - Flown guard should stop task 37 t2's illegal NQNU5R cancel. VERIFIED it fires on NQNU5R and NOT on the gold cancels Z7GOZK (19) / K1NW8N (23); no passing task cancels.
  - dob auto-fill lets a name change (task 40) go through without the user's dob; VERIFIED it reproduces gold pax for 3RK2T9 and is a no-op when dob is supplied. No passing task uses this tool.
  - The prompt rules are additive knowledge; the only ACT-leaning one (conditional go-ahead) is gated behind eligibility, and the cancel rule NARROWS refusal — neither loosens a global permission.
- Building on prior RESULTS: cand_0001 (ACCEPTED, +0.200) added payment auto-fill + enriched write returns + execute-on-confirmation prose. I did NOT re-touch book_reservation / update_reservation_flights (preserving those wins) and did NOT re-add more execute-on-yes prose (its unresolved tasks show prose alone is weak on that class per the tools skill) — I switched clusters to reservation-selection, cancel-gating, and passenger-fill, which cand_0001 explicitly left for a later iteration.
- Refuted hypotheses: none proven yet (only cand_0001 measured, and it neither broke nor measurably fixed anything).
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: yes+###STOP### confirm-then-no-write (8 t2, 23 t1) appears to be a simulator artifact (no post-confirmation turn) — only indirectly addressed; task 37 IFOYYZ ineligible-but-not-flown cancel can't be code-gated (cancel takes no reason arg), left to the prompt gate.
- Plateau signal: n/a (2nd iteration). If this batch's RESULT shows 17/22 still fail despite list_reservations, the next lever is a code `find_reservation(user_id, origin, destination)` resolver with a metro-area city map (EWR/JFK/LGA → "New York") so matching is deterministic rather than reasoned.
- Focus next iteration: read this RESULT; if accepted, do NOT re-propose these edits; target whatever cluster still shows a low mean (likely the ###STOP### / cheapest-enumeration ones).

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.567 Δ=+0.083 · fixed={—} · broke={—} · unresolved={11, 12, 19, 37, 40, 8} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them). — no task that was passing under the parent regressed: this batch did not clear the gate's threshold, it did not do damage. So the lever is POWER or SIZE, not a redesign — re-measure with more trials in ONE evaluation, or make the effect bigger. Keep the edits that produced the `fixed` tasks above as your starting point; do not rewrite them on this round's numbers.
